newsitem.title: USA: Gillette reports 15 percent increase in profits.
newsitem.headline: Gillette reports 15 percent increase in profits.

text.p: Gillette Co. reported a 15 percent increase in second-quarter profits Thursday and said it would launch a new product later this year that would be a "quantum improvement" in shaving.

The Boston-based consumer products giant reported net income of $318.9 million, or 57 cents a share, compared with $276.7 million, or 50 cents per share, in last year's second quarter. The earnings were in line with analysts'
expectations, according to the First Call service.
Total sales increased less than 1 percent to $2.29 billion from $2.27 billion.

In a conference call with analysts, Gillette spokesman Everett Howe said sales abroad were flat and that the strong dollar had shaved three percentage points from the company's sales growth in the quarter.

Howe said the company was continuing an inventory reduction in preparation for the launch of a new product that he described as a "quantum improvement in shaving" expected some time during the second half of the year.
He said the company was reducing backroom stock and that also adversely affected sales growth in the second quarter.
"Obviously, sales were weaker than expected (and) part of it was working down that inventory," said Edward Jones analyst Tony Vento.

Gillette also used the conference call to introduce a new disposable razor designed for women called Agility, which it expects to introduce in the United States late this year and and in Europe in March 1998.
The new product will be backed by a $5 million advertising campaign and will retail for about $3.49 for a package of four razors.
Gillette reported its quarterly earnings after markets closed. Earlier, its stock fell $2 to $101.375 on the New York Stock Exchange. "I think there was profit taking," said
Vento, "but the quality (in the numbers) was a little bit less than expected."
Gillette's stock in the second quarter rose from $78 to a high of $106.25.

Vento said the extremely strong showing was a "combination of the strength of the market and the strength in some of these global consumer product companies. Colgate, Proctor and Gamble, Coke have all done extraordinarily well this quarter and the leaders have all done extremely well. Gillette is obviously a leader."
